findings.reason: naming `reckon/review_tiers.py`/`reckon/path_classes.py` as the owner to extend decides where §4 lands and prevents a third duplicated figure-suffix set, which the live velocity copy shows is the drift risk.
findings.text: §4's selection predicate ("an image under a figures directory") is already owned by `file_class`/`path_class` in `reckon/path_classes.py` (returns "figures" for `docs/figures/` or a `FIGURE_SUFFIXES` extension) and consumed for artifact-based selection by `reckon/review_tiers.py:34,64`; the plan names neither, and `reckon/velocity.py:1976` already carries a second hardcoded copy of the same suffix set, so §4's implementation will add a third unless it is routed through the owner

findings.reason: the figure profile is a new tier/profile that review_tiers must produce; leaving it unmentioned risks a parallel selector beside the one the tier system already owns.
findings.text: the report path also records that §4's "selection by what the run wrote, never by the role" is the exact contract `reckon/review_tiers.py` already implements (`review_tier()` resolves a finished run from its changed paths), yet the plan attributes the rule only to scoring-plan §2g and to scoring-plan §6's plan-only write paths, so it does not connect the figure profile to the tier selector that must carry it

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design adds one slot (`input_modalities`) and one resolver, `reckon/flight.py:1381 select_profile_backend`, which hides the profile→required-modality→named-refusal path behind a single call and introduces no parallel module; the interface is smaller than what it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4 selects the figure profile by "changed an image under a figures directory" but cites a plan section (§2g) as the rule and names no code owner, while the predicate already lives in `reckon/path_classes.py` and its consumer `reckon/review_tiers.py`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the machinery it extends rather than rebuilds it: the codex `-i/--image` flag the dialect emits at `reckon/_backends.py`, `BackendConfig`'s slot set, the LinkML source at `reckon/schema/flight.yaml`, and the profile resolver `select_profile_backend`, so the "capability already exists" claim is checked against code and holds.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §2 extends the existing argv composition (`launch_plan` and each dialect's `argv()` in `reckon/_backends.py`) with an `images` argument; the codex dialect already carries `-i`, so this threads an existing capability rather than wrapping one, and the plan states why a dialect that cannot carry an image must raise rather than drop it.
